challenge.method: Checked the OSI label against the record's modification time, title and canonical link. Inspected each SPDX cross-reference's own match value. Compared the directly acquired tag object's tag, target type and target SHA with the commit in the detail, plain and template URLs. Considered a wrong tag, a different target, a supplied release label alone and the absence of a signature.
challenge.results: SPDX cites /license/MIT and OSI publishes /license/mit. The title and identifier support the named correspondence. The X.Org entry carries the string 'false' and the OSI entry carries 'N/A' for match. Neither supplies a positive text-match finding. A wrong tag or target would defeat release attribution, and a label alone would leave it unverified. The official object directly records the claimed mapping. Its unsigned status limits signer authentication. The documentary and observational tag acquisitions represent one SPDX authority.

limitations: The OSI label applies to the CMS revision modified 2026-11-24T10:18:15Z. Earlier archival identity and terms require evidence from that earlier revision.

The records establish documentary correspondence. Their wording differs, including OSI's singular COPYRIGHT HOLDER placeholder and SPDX's plural copyright holders. A particular project's license grant requires evidence from that project.

The review used the supplied SCES-1.0 identification at ab26f278422772f2d9e5d4dd016407d14372a710, bundle SHA-256 14da3f31f697ab828d4a4560f060dbe511861020db54bea7bc531e20ea0855ce. The permitted acquisitions did not include the bundle itself.
